data.title: Cyberpunk Apartment and Neon Block
data.summary: Sci-fi noir apartment models: modular block walls, floors and ceilings, capsule pods, a fold down bed, a multi screen desk, a compact kitchen, a wash pod, a server rack, a drone pad, neon signs with blank faces, balcony cages and rooftop plant.
data.description: A dense, lived in residential block for a sci-fi noir city, built to furnish a subdivided apartment, the corridor outside it and the neon face of the building. The shell is modular: 1.2 by 2.7 m wall modules dressed on both faces in four finishes, plain, service panelled, tiled and bare concrete corridor with its pipe run, plus an apartment door with a lit but deliberately blank number plate, a powered sliding security door with a keypad, a window wall with fixed blinds and a vending machine built into a wall panel, on 1.2 m floor tiles plain and with a drain grate, under 1.2 m ceiling panels. The circulation is there too: a lift door pair, a stair flight and landing, a rubbish chute, a magnetic lock, a wall camera, an intercom, a meter bank, a pipe riser, a service floor hatch and two graffiti panels. Inside a cell: a capsule sleeping pod open and shut, a two tier bunk, a fold down wall bed, a modular sofa bay, a low table, a task chair, a desk under a four screen rig, a wall display, a holo plinth with an abstract volume, a noodle cup shelf, a compact kitchen with a sink and hot plate, a glass front drinks fridge, a moulded wash pod, a stacked washer and dryer, a crate wall bay, a mat and a shoe rack. The work corner adds a server cabinet, a cable bundle, a bench with a soldering station, parts trays, a drone on its charge pad, a prosthetic arm on a stand, a medical kit, a stim cabinet of abstract vials, an air scrubber, a ducting section, an extract fan grille and a gun locker standing open and empty. Outside: neon raceways, blank faced sign frames, a lantern strip, a caged balcony with a drying rail, a condenser box, a satellite dish, a water tank, an antenna mast, a puddle plate and a bin cluster. Doors, drawers, lids, flaps, the sliding leaves, the fold down bed, the fans, the drone rotors and the camera head are named nodes on their own pivots with rigid open, close, spin and tilt clips: node transforms only, no skinning and no people. What does not move is as deliberate: the neon and every screen and readout are emissive materials rather than lights or displays, the cable bundles and drops hang in one fixed loop, the ducting is fixed plant, the blinds are set at one tilt, and the steam and the projected holo volume are geometry in an emissive material. Light, display content, a flexible run and a fluid each need a shader or a joint per element, and none of them is reachable with one rigid node transform, so this pack states them rather than faking them. No file embeds a light source. Nothing here carries a logo, wordmark, marque or readable text in any script: every sign field, screen, vending front, number plate, meter face and graffiti tag is blank or an invented geometric shape, so no real corporation, game, film or franchise is named or implied. Every file is self-contained CC0 geometry with no collision or navigation data.

starterScene.description: Four rented cells of a subdivided block on their own 1.2 m floor tiles, 21.6 by 13.2 m, built as an OPEN TOPPED cutaway: full wall runs stand between the cells and around them, but nothing is roofed except one bay of the service corridor, so a visitor walks the plot and looks straight down into every room. From the back: the shared corridor with the lift doors, the stair core, the rubbish chute, the meter bank, the intercom, a camera, a bin cluster, graffiti and two runs of neon along the wall. Through the party wall, three apartment doors and one sliding security door open into the cells. The left cell sleeps five: two capsule pods with a third stood open, a two tier bunk, a fold down wall bed, a laundry stack, a crate wall, a mat and a shoe rack. The second is the living cell: a three bay modular sofa round a low table with a swivel chair, a desk under a four screen rig, a wall display, a holo plinth, the compact kitchen with its hot plate, a drinks fridge and the noodle cup shelf. The third is the work cell: the bench with its soldering station and parts trays, a server cabinet and its cable spaghetti, a drone on a charge pad, a prosthetic arm on its stand, a medical kit, a stim cabinet, an air scrubber and an open, empty gun locker beside a shut one. The fourth is the utility cell: the wash pod, a second laundry stack, a crate run, a floor hatch, a pipe riser, a ducting run overhead and a fan grille. In front of the window wall, three caged balconies with drying rails and condenser boxes, and beyond them the street face: neon signs with blank faces, lantern strips, graffiti, puddles, bins and the block plant set down in the yard at the right hand end, the water tank, the antenna mast and the dish, where a walkthrough can reach them.

assets.description: Four rented cells of a subdivided block on their own 1.2 m floor tiles, 21.6 by 13.2 m, built as an OPEN TOPPED cutaway: full wall runs stand between the cells and around them, but nothing is roofed except one bay of the service corridor, so a visitor walks the plot and looks straight down into every room. From the back: the shared corridor with the lift doors, the stair core, the rubbish chute, the meter bank, the intercom, a camera, a bin cluster, graffiti and two runs of neon along the wall. Through the party wall, three apartment doors and one sliding security door open into the cells. The left cell sleeps five: two capsule pods with a third stood open, a two tier bunk, a fold down wall bed, a laundry stack, a crate wall, a mat and a shoe rack. The second is the living cell: a three bay modular sofa round a low table with a swivel chair, a desk under a four screen rig, a wall display, a holo plinth, the compact kitchen with its hot plate, a drinks fridge and the noodle cup shelf. The third is the work cell: the bench with its soldering station and parts trays, a server cabinet and its cable spaghetti, a drone on a charge pad, a prosthetic arm on its stand, a medical kit, a stim cabinet, an air scrubber and an open, empty gun locker beside a shut one. The fourth is the utility cell: the wash pod, a second laundry stack, a crate run, a floor hatch, a pipe riser, a ducting run overhead and a fan grille. In front of the window wall, three caged balconies with drying rails and condenser boxes, and beyond them the street face: neon signs with blank faces, lantern strips, graffiti, puddles, bins and the block plant set down in the yard at the right hand end, the water tank, the antenna mast and the dish, where a walkthrough can reach them.
